case_summary.summary: Patients were reported as falling off (disappearing from) the Status Board, with related symptoms such as a bed controller showing no patient admitted and being unable to suppress safety alerts. Investigation traced the behavior to how A08 and A02 HL7 ADT messages were being used to admit and move patients, which did not match the system's intended workflow. The case was closed on customer guidance recommending the correct use of A01/A08 for admissions and A02 for transfers.
case_summary.reported_issue: Patients were disappearing from the Status Board despite still being present in their rooms.
case_summary.product: Status Board / HL7 ADT patient admission and transfer messaging
case_summary.actions_taken: Reviewed rooms where patients were reported missing from Status Board and checked recent transfer messages
Found a Patient Staff Service log error indicating a patient was already active in a location
Rebooted a GRS7 device via putty after it failed to recognize an admitted patient, restoring safety alert suppression
Reviewed the HL7 message workflow for admissions (A08 and A01) and transfers (A02) against how the site was using them
Identified that A08 messages were being used for both new admissions and location updates, which does not move a patient between locations
case_summary.resolution: Customer guidance was provided: use A01 or A08 for new admissions and A02 for transferring existing patients between locations, which matches how the system processes these message types.
case_summary.status: resolved
case_summary.key_points: Cause code recorded as closed on customer request
A08 is not a transfer message in this configuration; A02 is required to move an existing patient between locations
A GRS7 device failed to recognize an admitted patient until rebooted, temporarily blocking suppression of a Bed Exit safety alert

investigation_details: We found that the customer was sending an A01 (update) message before sending an A08 (admit) message.   The same master patient id was used for both messages. The customer stopped sending the A01 in front of an A08 and that fixed the issue.

The patient is not showing up in Smart Client
troubleshooting_results: There is a workaround where i can edit the A01 (Admit) and make it an A02 (Transfer) and reprocess the message and the patient will show up (sometimes I have to update the date/time of the messages as well). While that is a workaround, it does not solve why this is happening in the first place. The hospital is demanding to know what is going on before continuing their testing or going live in Production with this new unit.
rca_review_comments: Customer fixed ADT messages on their end, this fixed the issue.

root_cause_summary: Revising this to a defect.  We made a change that allows a patient to be fully admitted and become active on an INFO action even if they do not have an assigned location.  This means that when the A01 comes thru to admit them it will be rejected because this patient is active in the system.  

The below is no longer accurate but is being left here for continuity.   
ADT message are being used incorrectly.  Customer messages are A08 (patient update) followed by A01 (admit patient to healthcare facility).  The A08 will make the patient active in our system, essentially admiting them without a location if none is provided.  When the A01 arrives the patient is detected as already admitted and to avoid admitting the same patient twice, the message is logged and rejected.  An A02 (transfer patient) would move the patient into a location.
investigation_details: if a patient is already active, whether or not they are in a HR location/bed, an A01 message, or ADMIT, will be rejected because the patient is already active.  an A02, transfer, is the correct message to move the patient from one location to another or into a location once they are active.  

Further, it seems like subsequent attempts were made with modified MRNs in a few cases.  These MRNs had a '.' prepeneded to them.  These rows need to have their MRN changed to remove the '.' and any other missing information for that patient added.

(convert the messages into discharge and then convert it into a cancel discharge, we can then admit the patient)

description: SB is not displaying accurate patient transfer information.  Smart Client/GRS-10 etc are accurate and up to date but SB is showing stale data.
comment_summary: Status Board did not reflect patient transfer information. Investigation found a problem introduced in the Bridge Service in 3.9.300: the Admit Patient message includes a null check that defaults missing values to an empty string before the message is sent, but Transfer and Swap messages do not. When a patient is admitted in Smart Client without some name fields, those values are stored as empty strings, whereas the ADTIntegrationService converts them to NULL before sending to the patient staff service, so NULL is persisted and the defect only appears on ADT transfers. The immediate solution chosen was a database trigger that replaces inserted NULL values with empty strings on patient admission and update, covering Smart Client and A01/A08 messages, and the decision for already-affected patients was to let them age out naturally through discharge rather than run a SQL correction script.

summary: NNC - 4.1.101 - Mirth not Assigning Preadmitted Patients to Assigned Rooms
description: Customer encountering an issue when transferring a preadmitted patient to a room.  
  
Using ControlID Q3165584123T4304834494X114724 in Mirth to examine what is going on, we are seeing the following:

1. A preadmit message enters the system as an A08 message and enters the patient into our database without a room assignment
2. Once it is decided to admit the patient, they are then transferred to a room with an A01 message. The system appears to ignore this message, as the transfer message is present and recognized by Mirth, but no changes are made in the database
3. The same goes for an ORU message attempting to assign a Falls Risk to this patient.

The end results is a failure to assign a falls risk to the room, and Status Board and Smart Client not displaying the patient's info. We ended up re-running the message transferring the patient to their room as an A02, which caused it to hit the database.
root_cause_summary: Functioning as expected/designed
investigation_details: The behavior noted above is how the code is written and is not a bug.  The A01/Admit code path checks to see if there is an active patient (checks by MasterPatientID and IsActive flag) and if there is it will log an Info level message that there is already an active patient at that location.   Because of the inclusion of the location information, I would say the pre-admit without a location scenario was not considered and should be discussed.  
  
Also, the ORU message does update the risks for that patient in the database.  It does not put the patient into a room.
verification_summary: No problem found.

summary: ADT INFO will admit patient when they have no location
description: an ADT INFO action can result in a patient being admitted if they are not active in our system.  Prior to August 2021, and after March of 2019, there was a check for a valid location prior to allowing an INFO to admit a patient.   
Some EMR systems will send an A08 prior to an A01 /ADMIT as part of their workflow.  Often the A08/INFO does not have location information as that comes later with the A01.  What we end up with is the A08 causing the patient to be admitted with no location and then the A01 gets rejected because the patient is already active and we reject all A01/ADMIT for an already active patient to avoid double admission.  Now, we’ve got essentially orphaned patients with no location and no easy way to discharge them. 

---

## Task Description

* GOAL: Fix code that prevents an ADT-A01 (ADMIT) from processing due to a previous ADT-A08 (INFO) having already been processed.
* BACKGROUND: A change to the `PatientStaffService` was made so that when an ADT-A08 is processed it will perform an ADMIT action (TACO-5406). However, some hospital EMR’s use an ADT-A08 as a “Pre-Admit” (instead of using an ADT-A04. In these hospitals they will send an ADT-A08 then later send an ADT-A01.  
    
  The processing of ADT messages can be complicated due to the business rules that we have implemented. Currently, when the ADT-A01 comes across it first checks to see if the “Master Patient ID” is “active” and if it is then it logs a message (“An active patient is already admitted at location…) and continues – basically ignoring the admit (“dropping it on the floor”).  
    
  I believe the fix may be to do one of the following:  
  \# 1. Augment the call to Patient.IsMasterPatientIdActive to include the location or action  
  \# 2. Add logic to the PatientADTService.ProcessAdmitAction so that it checks to see if the location is not set and the action is “ADMIT”, then we should merge the information and continue with the ADMIT action (need to check with Bill T to be sure there are no adverse issues)  
* CONSTRAINTS:

    * Minimal changes to the existing code base
    * 
    
* ASSUMPTIONS:

    * Automation suite will cover the formal testing
    * With this specific scenario the plan is that the A08 (treated as an admit) will be to a non-Baxter location. And the A01 will be to a Baxter location. This will be treated as a “Transfer” of the patient.
    * The issue that Michael N is having seems different from the brief explanation that I got from JVA.
    
        
comment_summary: The defect is that an ADT INFO message will admit a patient who has no location. The proposed handling was to treat an incoming A01 admit as a transfer when the patient is already present in Nurse Call for any reason, and to ignore an A08 information update as a pre-admission message when it has no PV1 assigned location and the patient is not active in the database. The regression was traced to earlier changes made on the Nurse Call side and the Mirth side under two linked tickets. A field workaround of altering the Mirth ADT channel to set the actionType to XFER when it resolves to ADMIT was proposed but flagged as needing validation on all versions from 4.1.000 and as risking loss of configured patient risks when Nurse Call receives a transfer. The issue was reported live at a customer with a patient safety concern, an RCA was opened, and the upgrade team sought a way to assess which customers would be affected; the code change broke several automated tests that were fixed and re-executed, and all planned tests eventually passed.

comment_summary: A Duress Alert placed from a Linq badge appears to be sent twice in rapid succession. Analysis of the logs shows two Duress events arriving roughly 75ms apart for the same location, with the Locating Service logs lacking detail and the Message Service logs showing a CallID of 0 on the second event, suggesting the second Duress published over RabbitMQ was associated with a database INSERT failure that did not stop delivery because of behavior added years ago after a transaction log overflow stopped PubSub processing. The thread reasons that the second Duress likely arrived while the first was still being processed, preventing the duplicate-detection logic from catching it, and notes that Messaging Service determines alert uniqueness from the CallID rather than the CallGuid, so two different CallIDs were treated as two different notifications. A further Duress test was captured with the HillRom.LocatingServiceHost log set to trace, and the thread raises a possible relationship to a more extreme case at another site covered by a separate defect.

comment_summary: Calls intermittently failed to clear from the Status board at sites running 4.1.200, severely enough that one customer paused remaining upgrade projects. Device Service Host logs for a stuck call showed the de-duplication logic failing to trigger, producing a SQL error 2601 "Cannot insert duplicate key row in object 'NCC.V_ActiveCall' with unique index 'AK_UniqueActiveCallGUID'" so call creation was abandoned, after which every subsequent status update (Answered, Cancel) failed with SQL error 257 "Implicit conversion from data type nvarchar to timestamp is not allowed" and the call never cleared. The suspicion was that a secondary or monitoring console reports the alert with the same BaseCallID but a different RequestingDeviceId, causing IsDuplicateAlertNotification() in AlertMessageHandler.cs to fail, and the affected units all used secondary consoles and unit monitoring. A separate bug was also found in the call_update stored procedure, where the row edition check compares @RowEdition to itself rather than to the stored RowEdition. The workaround that resolved it was setting MaxNumMessageProcessingThreads to 1 in the Device Service appsettings.json file, after which no further stuck-call reports were made at either site.

root_cause_summary: The root cause of this issue is unknown. The most likely cause is a race condition with the processing threads on the Mirth server that ended up freezing up the impacted customers channels. Other potential causes have been eliminated. The CPU/RAM and Memory on the Mirth server look healthy at the time of the incident and not every customer was impacted, which eliminates most issues with the Mirth VM itself. Another thought was a potential database issue, but restarting the channels resolved the issue with no further action taken to clear up database space, which makes that unlikely. If this happens again, we know what to check on the Mirth server to verify this being a processing threads race condition, but with no clear way to recreate the issue, we ultimately can't confirm the cause.
investigation_details: RabbitMQ nodes looked healthy and all up and functional, along with the federations. Next we looked to Mirth, where I found that a number of customers (six total, including the three in the RCA) were beginning to queue up. In the channels for these customers, I found that they were up and actively receiving and queueing messages, but were not processing anything new. The last processed message in any of these customers channels was about the same time (7:16am). 

To try and resolve this, I restarted the ADT channels for these customers. After they came up again, they all began processing messages again. While messages had queued up for a few hours (we resolved this issue around 9:30am), most customers had cleared and were caught up to normal again by the early afternoon.
verification_summary: Root cause inconclusive. After restarting ADT, messages started to process. Further investigation would be needed if issue were to recur.
rca_review_comments: If this happens again, we know what to check on the Mirth server to verify this being a processing threads race condition, but with no clear way to recreate the issue, we ultimately can't confirm the cause. We have monitored Mirth the past week since the incident and this has not happened again.

summary: Race Condition with Call creation from monitored units
description: https://baxter-international.atlassian.net/browse/RCA-1625   
  
When units are being monitored, the system will report multiple of the same call (GUID/BaseCallID) to the Device Service, one from the NUC of the unit where the call was generated, and N number of calls from the Consoles that are monitoring the NUC.  The system will add the call to the SQL database and then onto an in-memory list.  The system will look on the in-memory list to determine if a call that has been reported has already been raised.  Occasionally the 2nd notification of the call will come in before the injection into SQL and adding onto the in-memory list has finished occurring.  This race condition will cause the system to incorrectly identify the monitoring console’s report as a new call.  This will fail to process and eventually result in a call that is stuck in both the database and StatusBoard (RabbitMQ specifically).  
  
In the customer environment, they have a separate SQL server and other external factors that could contribute to this race condition occurring that would have to be emulated for testing.

Development stated the potential race condition has existed since 2012, with no explanation yet for why it only appeared with 4.1.200 and why not all 4.1.200 sites see it, and noted the same change must also be made in the cc-nc-lib-alertComponent repository. A SQL loop repeatedly selecting from dbo.call with a half second delay was used to put load on the system while attempting reproduction. The defect could not be reproduced on PDR0 and the direct test P1575-TEST-3707 passed there after being blocked in PDP28.

impact_description: Impact Assessment Summary:  
Moving the default value from 2 to 1 for the MaxNumMessageProcessingThreads in the appsettings.json and code causes the service to only process 1 message at a time.  This allows the system to avoid the race condition while minimizing code changes/regression.  
Before: Failure to process a SQL Insert before a monitored NUC reports a call results in calls incorrectly being identified as a new call instead of a duplicate, throwing errors in the DeviceService log and having the calls stuck in the DB & on StatusBoard.  
After: Device Service correctly identifies the calls as duplicates.  
Impact Assessment:  
NCP - Error Handling and System Alerting - Trivial  
Platform Impact:  
N/A  
Regression Meeting:  
Date:  27/OCT/2025  
Attendees - Josh Watkins (Development Engineering), Kate Papalava (Quality Engineering)  
Minutes - The call processing logic is not impacted by the change, so the direct test is sufficient for verification.  
Additional Software Components:  
N/A
steps_taken: 1\. Configure a console to monitor another unit for Normal Calls.  
2\. Set up a method to prevent the SQL call completing before the 2nd notification comes in.  
3\. Place a normal call from a monitored location.
actual_results: The system treats the 2nd notification as a new call, causing SQL errors in the Device Service log and the call is stuck in the database and in Statusboard.
expected_results: The system should detect that the 2nd notification is a duplicate and not re-process the call.

comment_summary: Calls intermittently failed to clear from the Status board at sites running 4.1.200, severely enough that one customer paused remaining upgrade projects. Device Service Host logs for a stuck call showed the de-duplication logic failing to trigger, producing a SQL error 2601 "Cannot insert duplicate key row in object 'NCC.V_ActiveCall' with unique index 'AK_UniqueActiveCallGUID'" so call creation was abandoned, after which every subsequent status update (Answered, Cancel) failed with SQL error 257 "Implicit conversion from data type nvarchar to timestamp is not allowed" and the call never cleared. The suspicion was that a secondary or monitoring console reports the alert with the same BaseCallID but a different RequestingDeviceId, causing IsDuplicateAlertNotification() in AlertMessageHandler.cs to fail, and the affected units all used secondary consoles and unit monitoring. A separate bug was also found in the call_update stored procedure, where the row edition check compares @RowEdition to itself rather than to the stored RowEdition. The workaround that resolved it was setting MaxNumMessageProcessingThreads to 1 in the Device Service appsettings.json file, after which no further stuck-call reports were made at either site.

When units are being monitored, the system will report multiple of the same call (GUID/BaseCallID) to the Device Service, one from the NUC of the unit where the call was generated, and N number of calls from the Consoles that are monitoring the NUC. impact_description: Impact Assessment Summary:  
Moving the default value from 2 to 1 for the MaxNumMessageProcessingThreads in the appsettings.json and code causes the service to only process 1 message at a time.  This allows the system to avoid the race condition while minimizing code changes/regression.  
Before: Failure to process a SQL Insert before a monitored NUC reports a call results in calls incorrectly being identified as a new call instead of a duplicate, throwing errors in the DeviceService log and having the calls stuck in the DB & on StatusBoard.  
After: Device Service correctly identifies the calls as duplicates.

N/A

Minutes - The call processing logic is not impacted by the change, so the direct test is sufficient for verification.

root_cause_summary: The root cause of this issue is unknown. The most likely cause is a race condition with the processing threads on the Mirth server that ended up freezing up the impacted customers channels. Other potential causes have been eliminated. The CPU/RAM and Memory on the Mirth server look healthy at the time of the incident and not every customer was impacted, which eliminates most issues with the Mirth VM itself. Another thought was a potential database issue, but restarting the channels resolved the issue with no further action taken to clear up database space, which makes that unlikely. If this happens again, we know what to check on the Mirth server to verify this being a processing threads race condition, but with no clear way to recreate the issue, we ultimately can't confirm the cause.
investigation_details: RabbitMQ nodes looked healthy and all up and functional, along with the federations. Next we looked to Mirth, where I found that a number of customers (six total, including the three in the RCA) were beginning to queue up. In the channels for these customers, I found that they were up and actively receiving and queueing messages, but were not processing anything new. The last processed message in any of these customers channels was about the same time (7:16am). 

To try and resolve this, I restarted the ADT channels for these customers. After they came up again, they all began processing messages again. While messages had queued up for a few hours (we resolved this issue around 9:30am), most customers had cleared and were caught up to normal again by the early afternoon.
verification_summary: Root cause inconclusive. After restarting ADT, messages started to process. Further investigation would be needed if issue were to recur.
rca_review_comments: If this happens again, we know what to check on the Mirth server to verify this being a processing threads race condition, but with no clear way to recreate the issue, we ultimately can't confirm the cause. We have monitored Mirth the past week since the incident and this has not happened again.
